state:
Follow-up architecture decisions for a Go + SQLite Telegram-to-web document archive imitating Papra.

Previously decided (Jev, earlier round): long polling, go-telegram/bot, metadata-only storage (file bytes stay in Telegram), Go html/template + htmx, vanilla CSS with shadcn-style tokens, modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go), single-tenant, optional ADMIN_PASSWORD gate, dark-first Papra-inspired look (~3.5/6 fidelity).

NEW verified facts from Papra's actual source code (user now asks the tagging engine be as close to Papra's as possible):
- Operators: equal, not_equal, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with.
- Condition: field + operator + value + isCaseSensitive (per-condition flag).
- Fields in Papra: name and content. We ingest Telegram documents; filename, extension, and mime type are available cheaply. Extracting text content from pdf/docx would need extra parsing libraries and OCR is out of scope.
- Rule: conditionMatchMode all (default) or any; actions = MULTIPLE tags per rule (earlier single-tag decision predates this); no conditions = rule matches everything; a failing condition never blocks ingestion.
- Papra has an 'Apply to existing documents' background task re-running one rule over the whole archive with stats.

Environment: user will test on a Windows PC first, then deploy with Docker; the app must be a single Go binary, no Node/TypeScript build step; SQLite via modernc driver; Telegram bot long polling.

rule_fields.instructions: Which condition fields should the rule engine support in v1, given Papra has name+content but content extraction from pdf/docx adds heavy dependencies?

criteria.name_only: Only filename conditions; least surface, but weaker than Papra.
criteria.name_ext_mime: Filename + extension + mime type; all cheap metadata, near-Papra power without parsing libraries.
criteria.name_content: Filename + extracted text content like Papra; requires pdf/docx text extraction libraries, big scope increase.

multi_tag_actions.instructions: Should a rule's action be able to apply multiple tags (Papra parity), superseding the earlier single-tag-per-rule decision?

criteria.true: Yes, actions apply one or more tags like Papra.
criteria.false: No, keep one tag per rule.

retag_feature.instructions: How should re-applying rules to already-archived documents be exposed in the UI?

criteria.per_rule_run_now: A 'Run now' button per rule, like Papra's 'Apply to existing documents', with a processed/tagged report.
criteria.global_button: One global 'Re-run all rules' button; simpler but less precise.
criteria.both: Per-rule 'Run now' plus a global re-run button.

case_default.instructions: Should conditions default to case-insensitive (isCaseSensitive=false), matching the user's 'case agnostic' requirement and Papra's per-condition flag defaulting to insensitive?

criteria.true: Default case-insensitive, with a per-condition case-sensitive checkbox.

ui_layout.instructions: Which overall layout should the Papra-style web UI use?

criteria.sidebar: Papra-like left sidebar (Documents, Tagging Rules) with a main content area; closer to Papra.
criteria.topbar: Simple top navigation bar; lighter, more Telegram-ish.

docker_now.instructions: Should the Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml be created now (even though the user will test on Windows first), so deployment is ready right after local testing?

criteria.true: Create Dockerfile + compose now; test locally on Windows before building the image.
criteria.false: Defer Docker files until after Windows testing.

tests_depth.instructions: What level of automated tests should be written for the Go backend on day one?

criteria.rules_only: Unit tests for the rule engine only (operator semantics, match modes, case sensitivity), mirroring Papra's own test cases.
criteria.rules_store: Rule engine plus SQLite store integration tests.
